newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria offers Bosnian refugees cash to go home.
newsitem.headline: Austria offers Bosnian refugees cash to go home.

text.p: Austria will offer Bosnian refugee families living in the country up to 25,000 schillings ($2,070) each to return home, Chancellor Viktor Klima said on Friday.
In a statement, Klima said only a small part of the sum would be paid in cash, with most being earmarked for reconstruction and infrastructure projects in war-shattered Bosnia.
The government said it expected about half of the estimated 11,000 Bosnian refugees living in Austria to make use of the offer, jointly financed by the federal and state governments.
"This is a voluntary offer, which will improve the starting position of those who are willing to return but also will help the communities to which they will return," Klima said.
The offer is valid from mid-March to August 1997.
The number of Bosnians living in Austria has dropped significantly from the estimated 90,000 who sought refuge in the Alpine republic at the height of the 43-month Bosnian war.
The proposal was strongly criticised by Austria's far-right opposition. Joerg Haider, leader of the Freedom Party, told state television: "Cash gifts don't achieve anything."
In an interview published on Thursday, Haider said he wanted one third of all foreigners working in Austria to be sent home over the next two years to ease the strain on the labour market.
Austrian unemployment hit 300,000 in January, the highest level since World War Two. ($ = 12.05 Austrian Schillings)
